Move date: ____________  Oregon address: __________________________

DOCUMENTS — KEEP IN THE CAR, NOT THE MOVING TRUCK
[ ] J  IDs, lease/closing papers, and important originals
[ ] M  Vehicle registration and insurance; title if needed for DMV
[ ] P  Moving estimate, bill of lading, inventory, and payment details

MOVER / TRUCK
[ ] P  Confirm pickup window, parking/access, and payment method
[ ] J  Check inventory and note existing damage; never sign blank forms
[ ] P  Keep signed copies; confirm delivery window or truck return details
Pickup: ______________  Delivery / truck return: ___________________

EMERGENCY CONTACTS — FILL IN BEFORE LEAVING
[ ] P  Mover / truck rental: ________________________________________
[ ] M  Roadside assistance / policy number: _________________________
[ ] M  Vet / 24-hour emergency vet: _________________________________
[ ] P  Landlord / property contact: _________________________________
[ ] P  Overnight lodging / backup contact: _________________________

FINAL WALK-THROUGH

[ ] P  Return keys, fobs, and remotes; get a receipt

turns.text:
# Ohio → Oregon: Phone Reminder Calendar

**Target move day: Thursday, July 16, 2026** (about 10 weeks out). Use the dates below as reminder anchors and shift them together if move day changes. **M** = me · **P** = partner · **J** = joint. **High** = deadline or dependency · **Medium** = useful but flexible.

**Phone setup:** Add each bold title to a shared reminders list, paste the line below it into the notes, and assign M/P items to the owner. For joint items, pick one person to mark them complete. If your lease notice or sale deadline comes before Week −8, set that reminder now.

### Week −8 · May 21
- **Book movers, truck, or container** — J · High  
  Compare written totals, verify interstate mover credentials, and check coverage, deposit, and cancellation terms before paying.
- **Confirm Oregon housing** — J · High  
  Lock in the key or closing date, or book dog-friendly temporary housing if there’s a gap.
- **Decide: drive or ship the car** — J · High  
  Compare shipping quotes with driving costs; reserve a carrier if shipping.
- **Book the dog’s vet visit** — M · High  
  Request vaccine records, a rabies certificate, and enough medication for the trip.

### Week −7 · May 28
- **Book dog-friendly overnights** — M · High  
  Confirm pet fees, size limits, and late check-in for each stop.
- **Reserve Oregon internet install** — P · Medium  
  Book for arrival week and check whether someone needs to be home.
- **Set the move budget** — J · Medium  
  Include deposits, travel, pet fees, temporary housing, and a contingency buffer.

### Week −6 · June 4
- **Declutter garage and closets** — J · Medium  
  Sort into keep, sell, donate, and discard; book a donation pickup if needed.
- **Gather paperwork for the car** — P · High  
  Pull together IDs, housing papers, vehicle records, mover documents, and vet records.
- **Check Oregon DMV requirements** — M · High  
  Verify new-resident deadlines, title or lienholder paperwork, and any address-based emissions test.

### Week −5 · June 11
- **Pack storage and off-season items** — J · Medium  
  Start with décor, books, and spare linens; label each box by room and priority.
- **Schedule car maintenance** — M · High  
  Get tires, brakes, battery, and fluids checked before departure.
- **Confirm move-out handoff** — P · High  
  Book the inspection or closing handoff and confirm where to return keys and fobs.

### Week −4 · June 18
- **Schedule utility and insurance dates** — P · High  
  Keep Ohio utilities on through handoff; start Oregon utilities and renters or homeowners coverage by key day.
- **Check loading and delivery access** — P · High  
  Reserve elevators or parking as needed and confirm the truck can access both addresses.
- **Pack guest room and spare kitchenware** — J · Medium  
  Leave a basic cooking and bedding kit out for the final weeks.

### Week −3 · June 25
- **Confirm dog care for loading day** — M · High  
  Book a sitter or plan a secure quiet room; test the travel crate or harness on a short drive.
- **Schedule service cancellations** — P · Medium  
  Set cable, trash, and local memberships to end when needed; note equipment return deadlines.
- **Finish donations and bulky pickups** — J · Medium  
  Clear sold or donated items before the mover’s final inventory.

### Week −2 · July 2
- **Set USPS forwarding and update accounts** — P · High  
  Choose the forwarding start date; update payroll, banks, insurers, and deliveries directly.
- **Reconfirm mover, truck, or carrier** — J · High  
  Verify pickup and delivery windows, payment method, and day-of contacts.
- **Confirm auto coverage for the move** — M · High  
  Ask your insurer when to switch the garaging address and Oregon policy so coverage stays continuous.

### Week −1 · July 9
- **Pack first-night bags and dog kit** — J · High  
  Keep meds, chargers, clothes, dog supplies, and the document pouch in the car.
- **Photograph valuables and inventory** — P · Medium  
  Save photos and serial numbers somewhere you can access from your phone.
- **Check route, fuel, and lodging** — M · High  
  Download offline maps, reconfirm dog-friendly stops, and set a night-before reminder to fuel up.
- **Set Oregon arrival reminders** — P · Medium  
  Add move-in photos, DMV deadlines, dog licensing and microchip updates, and Ohio equipment returns.

### Week 0 · July 16 — Move Day
- **Secure dog and stage the car kit** — M · High  
  Keep the dog away from loading; put documents, meds, water, and the essentials checklist in the car.
- **Check inventory and sign paperwork** — J · High  
  If using movers, note existing damage, keep signed copies, and reconfirm the delivery contact.
- **Do final sweep, meter reads, and keys** — P · High  
  Check every room, photograph final meter readings, and get a receipt for keys and fobs.
- **Fuel up and start the drive** — M · High  
  Check the fuel level, secure the dog in the car, and plan the first break within 2–3 hours.
